statement: Final episode of the alchemy bubble tier list; covers the Kazam cauldron (yellow bubbles).
Lotto Skill is a linear bubble giving luck and requires red material; it is total luck not base luck so all-stat percent does not scale it.
Lotto Skill cannot really be scaled: you can't hourly click it and it isn't worth using atoms on it.
Lotto Skill is top of C tier; of the four bubbles in its group it's not quite there.
Larry: chance for a bubble upgrade to apply twice for free; above 100% it can give +3. Takes dementia? material, easy to get.
Larry bubble is required for decent alchemy, easily S tier in his books.
Cogs for Hands: linear bubble giving percent cog production speed, costs frost flakes from early world 3.
Cogs for Hands is crucial for cog grinding but you don't start cog grinding until later game; low B tier.
Sample It gives sample size for 3D printer sampling and costs Dune Souls; scaling is terrible.
Only hard-prioritize Sample It when trying to drop Royal Sampler which is an endgame thing; otherwise no bubble left behind covers it.
Big Game Hunter must be equipped: killing a giant monster has 52% chance to not decrease giant mob spawn odds; resets weekly; costs scorpion.
Big Game Hunter is a super solid bubble but expensive; S tier-ish for active players.
Big Game Hunter pairs with the Titan-related prayer (taxation?) reducing giant mob chance; idle players won't benefit.
Ignore Overdues gives percent book checkout speed so library refreshes books faster; requires wispy lumber from Quenches.
Ignore Overdues is really good late game but can't be scaled or leveled early; depends on whether you get automation arm.
Yellow Bargain Tag lowers material cost of yellow bubbles by percent; it does not get multiplied unlike other bargain tags; costs pingies.
Yellow Bargain Tag goes at the bottom of the pack.
Mr Massacre gives multi-kill per damage tier not flat multi-kill; with 15 damage tiers on a mob the percentage stacks 15 times.
Mr Massacre costs blue salts? and is a world 4 bubble; hard for no bubble left behind to level; early scaling needed to make it strong.
Mr Massacre can be skipped alongside bargain tag; for mid game players it is top of its tier.
Egg Ink gives percent faster egg incubation in pet nest; helps egg rarity; requires first spice of breeding.
You're never going to prioritize Egg Ink; spices are very time gated and don't get good until you have converter pet.
Egg Ink placed below Lotto Skill.
Diamond Chef is a multiplier making meal and kitchen speed faster for every meal at 11 plus; costs beach dog? salts.
Diamond Chef is one of the biggest snowballs in cooking until enough plates for V-man enhancements; worth building a build to farm its salts, S tier.
Card drop chance for all card types including party dungeon cards; requires purple salts; additive, not multiplicative.
Card bubble is stupidly expensive for what it gives so placed C tier right above bargain tag.
Dropping Loads gives percent drop rate and requires goldfish only.
Dropping Loads scaling is bad at first but scales fast early to mid game; easy to cap out; top of A tier.
Petting the Rift gives percent shiny chance per new Rift level reached and costs blobfish.
Petting the Rift: by the time you can use it you'll have 1-to-1 shiny chance anyway; never focus it; leave at level one.
Booty Bubbles give sailing speed for all boats; costs bits? so not atomable.
Booty Bubbles are solid for early sailing but scale quickly and cap; almost A tier but top of B.
Big P multiplies the minor link bonus of your gods in Divinity; requires first sailing material.
Big P is a multiplier that helps minor god bonuses and scales okay; top of its tier.
Bit by Bit gives percent more bits earned in gaming; costs dandelion logs.
Bit by Bit scaling is less crazy and ramps slowly; placed right below Booty Bubbles in B tier.
Gifts Abound gives percent chance to not use up points when offering a gift; requires dust moths?; second to last bubble unlocked.
Gifts Abound has small infrequent proc; low C tier right above bargain tag.
Atom Split gives percent lower particle cost for upgrading atoms; costs tremor worms; omega late bubble; 6410 atoms at 1 billion?
Atom Split is C tier and not a priority.
Leveling a statue resets XP bar to two percent instead of zero; costs sand from sandy pots.
Solid overall bubble that saves hundreds to hundreds of thousands worth of statue levels; very cheap and easily scalable; toward bottom of pack.
Level Up Gift: percent chance to drop a gift on any level up (XP balloon, gem, fun flags); costs crab cake material; cheap early bubble.
Level Up Gift is top of C tier because it becomes completely useless late game.
Prowess bonus multiplier for skills; lowers efficiency needed for multiple quantities per drop; prowess caps at 2.0; costs soy logs.
Solid early to mid game but becomes a low C tier by early late game; put at bottom of its pack.
Stamp bubble raises max level of the Toilet Paper Postage star talent and potency of skilling stamps; linear +1 per level; costs butterflies.
Don't put points in the stamp bubble early game; prioritize Action Frenzy and Super Source and Frothy Milk instead.
Decently strong late game; very bottom of C tier.
Undeveloped Costs reduces material cost of alchemy bubbles by percentage; requires jellyfish.
Good early-to-mid discount but like other bargain tags becomes garbage late game since you'll get atoms ASAP; bottom of pack.
Daily Drip increases max cap of every liquid by a plus amount based on combined alchemy level of all characters; costs leather.
Daily Drip is very strong for max liquid, but only costs leather and isn't potent until later in game so placed in a mid-low tier.
Grind Time requires only liquids to level and gives XP; how you reach roughly x40 to x70 XP multiplier.
Grind Time is one of the best bubbles: one of the cheapest to level up and gives a reason to hyper farm it.
Stacking Grind Time with a couple cards makes it possible to get equipment and more talent points.
Grind Time is basically tied with Diamond Chef but scales higher so becomes better over time.
